$comment: Baseline for `pnpm rls:bypass-check` (scripts/check-tenant-bypass.ts).
This is a RATCHET, not a mute button. The gate is red when a key is missing
here (a new bypass), red when a key's count goes UP (a new call site on an
already-known file), and warns when a count goes DOWN (an entry someone fixed
and forgot to remove). `--prune` lowers the counts for you when work lands;
nothing lowers them silently.
kind = 'allowed'       the call site is correct as written and is expected to stay.
kind = 'system-scope'  the call site LEAVES its tenant scope on purpose, through
withSystemScope (src/lib/system-scope.ts), and the reason
is written down. CHECK D counts these.
kind = 'debt'          the call site is wrong; `card` names who closes it. The gate
prints the outstanding debt on every run, green or red, so a
deferred finding cannot go quiet the way the ones in
TASK-MTSHUZUMVLTBF did.
The kind and the check must agree: CHECK D entries are 'system-scope' and no
other check may be. Without that rule the sanctioned path WOULD be the mute
button — moving a call onto withSystemScope takes it out of CHECK A (the
accessor becomes `tx.`), so it has to land in CHECK D or it lands nowhere.
Measured on 2026-09-10 against dev by TASK-MTVTPVTEBCF5Z (slice 6).
Every reason below was read out of the file it names, not inferred from the
path. See docs/agent-results/TASK-MTVTPVTEBCF5Z-de-fb.md.
History: TASK-MTVRAZSUVLL9R recorded 31 'allowed' entries covering 35 call
sites. All 35 were correct as tenant scoping and returned ZERO ROWS under the
NOBYPASSRLS role fabrika_app — measured, not feared. Slice 6 moved them onto
the sanctioned path, where they became 22 call sites in 16 entries: batches
that shared a purpose were collapsed into one scope each (the GDPR export's
six reads, the erasure sweep's eight writes, the digest's two), and one turned
out to be plainly scopable and is now withTenant.
Every `debt` entry has a real card on the board:
TASK-MTVTMZXYT84RZ  wrap the two scopable billing calls (K1)
TASK-MTVSBEO7VX6Y4  the surviving subscription-sync fallback (that card owns the file)

entries.subject: system-scope:tenant-discovery
entries.reason: The SHA-256 key hash IS the credential and this lookup is what DISCOVERS the tenant, so withTenant cannot wrap it: the argument it needs is this call's result. Measured under fabrika_app: the unscoped read returns no row, so every API key on the platform stops authenticating. The lastUsedAt write that follows is now withTenant(keyRecord.tenantId) — only the read had to cross tenants.

entries.subject: system-scope:tenant-discovery
entries.reason: Magic-token partner portal: there is no session at all. The token is the credential and the row names its own tenant. Two call sites, generateMetadata and the page body, both reading the same row by magicToken. Same discovery shape as api-auth.ts.

entries.subject: system-scope:tenant-discovery
entries.reason: addBudgetLineByToken. The comment on the line says it: 'Resolved by token, then re-scoped to that row's own tenant for the write.' The read discovers the tenant; savePartContent(part.tenantId, ...) that follows is scoped.

entries.subject: system-scope:tenant-discovery
entries.reason: Answers 'which tenant does this signed-in user own?'. Scoped by session.user.id and role; the tenantId it returns is what createPortalSession is then given. Nothing narrower exists to scope to yet.

entries.subject: system-scope:tenant-discovery
entries.reason: findRecorded(): the idempotency lookup by providerEventId, which runs BEFORE the tenant is known — exactly the api-auth.ts shape. Empty under fabrika_app means every Stripe webhook retry is treated as a new sale.

entries.subject: system-scope:subject-scoped
entries.reason: GDPR Art. 15/20 portability export. ONE scope around the whole Promise.all batch, replacing six separate unscoped reads (user, membership, account, evaluation, effort, aiUsageLog, approvalRequest, opportunity): every row is selected by userId or ownerId across every tenant the data subject belongs to, and a single tenant scope would silently under-deliver the export. One transaction also makes the export a consistent snapshot.

entries.subject: system-scope:subject-scoped
entries.reason: Three GDPR Art. 17 reads. (1) The subject row WITH its nested `memberships` select — a nested read of the tenant-scoped Membership table obeys RLS exactly like a top-level one, so outside a scope it returns [] and the sole-owner warning below silently stops warning; this shape is invisible to CHECK A, which reads the accessor. (2) The sole-owner count, asked per tenant but for EVERY tenant the subject is in, one scope around the whole loop so N tenants do not mean N transactions. (3) cancelAccountDeletion listing the subject's tenants to revalidate them, where: { userId }.

entries.subject: system-scope:subject-scoped
entries.reason: The erasure sweep. (1) dueUsers, again for its nested `memberships` select: empty under fabrika_app means every erasure audit is written with no tenant attribution — a silently weaker audit trail, not an error. (2) One scope around the eight detach/delete statements, all `where: { userId }` with no tenantId anywhere, so scoping per tenant would mean enumerating tenants from the row set about to change. Under fabrika_app each reports count: 0 and the sweep announces a completed erasure having deleted nothing. One transaction also means a crash halfway cannot leave a half-erased person. The per-tenant erasure audit write is NOT here: it knows its tenant and now uses withTenant.

entries.subject: system-scope:platform-admin
entries.reason: Platform admins triage across tenants. The file states it and the route is gated by the admin layout; each action re-checks the role with requirePlatformAdmin(). Under fabrika_app the board renders an empty and entirely convincing 'no feedback' screen.

entries.subject: system-scope:platform-admin
entries.reason: The triage write behind requirePlatformAdmin(), updating one row by id in whichever tenant raised it. Under fabrika_app an unscoped update matches no row and Prisma raises P2025, so the console reports update_failed for every entry.

entries.subject: system-scope:platform-admin
entries.reason: The module console renders a tenant x module grid; the read is unfiltered on purpose and the page groups by s.tenantId afterwards. Under fabrika_app it returns nothing and every cell renders as 'off' — a wrong grid, not an empty one. Its former sibling in admin/modules/actions.ts turned out to be a different question (one named tenant) and is now plain withTenant, closing the proposed card K-2.

entries.subject: system-scope:platform-aggregate
entries.reason: Three counts about the whole estate, never about one tenant's rows: subscription.groupBy for 'how many live subscriptions does each plan have' (the platform plan console), and subscription.count twice — computePublishImpact and countLiveSubscriptions, both asking how many tenants a plan change would touch.

entries.subject: system-scope:platform-aggregate
entries.reason: The highest `seq` across the whole estate. The licence number is a platform-wide scarce resource capped at LIFETIME_LICENCE_CAP; under fabrika_app this reads null, every buyer is handed seq 1 and the cap stops counting.

entries.subject: system-scope:platform-aggregate
entries.reason: The function's own docstring: 'Reads the window and everything still open, both cross-tenant.' It builds the PLATFORM's beta digest, not a tenant's. One scope around the pair, so the two reads share a snapshot and the gate counts one escape.

entries.subject: system-scope:cross-tenant-job
entries.reason: Cron fan-out: reads every tenant's due relationship actions, then groups by focal point. The tenant set is the query's OUTPUT, so no single scope exists to run it in. Under fabrika_app it returns nothing, so the job mails no one and reports success.

entries.subject: system-scope:cross-tenant-job
entries.reason: Same fan-out shape: the daily job reads every tenant's alert-enabled saved searches before mailing each one. Empty under fabrika_app is reported as totalSearches: 0 — the false success the job's own docstring says it refuses.

entries.subject: subscription.findUnique
entries.reason: tenantId is already a parameter of this function — nothing discovers it, nothing aggregates. This is a plain unwrapped tenant read that slices 1-4 did not reach because src/lib/billing/** was fenced off for another card.

entries.subject: lifetimeLicence.create
entries.reason: Writes data: { tenantId, ... } with the tenant in hand. Unlike its two findFirst siblings in the same file this one is scopable, and under fabrika_app an unscoped INSERT is REFUSED by the WITH CHECK clause — a paid lifetime licence would fail to record.

entries.subject: tenantId-collapse-ternary
entries.reason: `...(tenantId ? { tenantId } : {})` on an auditEvent.create DATA object, not a where clause. AuditEvent.tenantId is String? (NULLABLE_TENANT since TASK-MTU6HUB8FUHMG C-2) and a tenant-less subject legitimately writes NULL; the spread omits a column rather than widening a filter. The rule is kept position-blind on purpose — deciding 'is this a where or a data' needs context the scanner does not have, and one documented exemption is cheaper than a rule that guesses.

entries.subject: tenantId-fallback
entries.reason: `tenantId: (subscription.metadata?.tenantId as string) ?? ''` in a logger.warn payload. The empty string is exactly what assertTenantScope rejects, so the log line names a tenant that can never be looked up. This file had TWO of these when the baseline was written; TASK-MTVSBEO7VX6Y4 removed the second (a `|| ''` in the handler's return value on the already-processed path) while this card was running, and the gate reported the fall as a warning rather than blocking that agent's push. The survivor belongs to the same card.
